newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on export optimism, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on export optimism, technicals.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on export action plus technical gains and nearby December rallied early to a new six-week high, traders said.
"It was mostly technical but there's business around with Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Pakistan," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

U.S. export sources also said the cash basis market for soft red winter wheat delivered to the Gulf increased 10-1/2 cents per bushel for prompt shipment which gave further credence to the export-related gains.
But technical factors were central to the gains.

Chart watchers said the key four and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals. The December contract broke through first resistance at $4.13-1/2 in early dealings and by midday had penetrated second resistance at $4.21-1/2 to set a session high of $4.22-1/2 where buying evaporated.
However, traders said the volume was thin which exacerbated the rally and also magnified the rapid decline from the day's highs near the close.
Wheat closed unchanged to 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with December up 5-1/2 at $4.15-3/4.

The market took note of Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report which showed funds remained net short wheat as of November 19. The CFTC said fund shorts totaled 46.24 million bushels and were long 32.92 million bushels.
News Turkey and the U.S. appear closer to resolving a trade dispute also was mentioned along with a report indicating China may be caving in on the TCK Smut issue.
Turkey and the U.S. are close to resolving issues that have been virtually banning U.S. wheat and other grain sales to Turkey in the past month, a USDA official said Monday.
Also, China's President Jiang Zemin said he will look into U.S. complaints about exclusion of U.S. wheat from China due to TCK smut fungus, Sen Dirk Kempthorne (R-Idaho) said Monday.

Traders also cited the firm cash basis markets domestically as supportive to wheat futures and the probable posting of no deliveries Friday against the December contract. Friday is first notice day for deliveries on CBOT December.

Weekly exports were slightly supportive with USDA Monday saying U.S. wheat inspected for export the week ended November 21 totaled 16.513 million bushels which was near the upper end of trade expectations for 13 million to 18 million bushels.

Buyers included commercials and speculators with Term Commodities purchasing one million bushels of March, FIMAT Futures bought two million March and Cargill Inc bought one half million March but sold one million in late dealings, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts, about on par with the 18,045 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Dean Witter Reynolds bought 500 July $3.50 calls at 18-1/2 cents, FIMAT Futures bought 400 March $3.90 calls and sold 400 July $3.60 calls at 10 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, above the 4,833 traded Friday.
